From 642023d04335458a057b549da329ee4e30c8a838 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sean Wang <sean.wang@mediatek.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2020 23:42:21 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] mt76: mt7615: fix up typo in Kconfig for MT7663U

Fix up typo in Kconfig with indicating MT7663U is an 802.11ac device

Fixes: eb99cc95c3b6 ("mt76: mt7615: introduce mt7663u support")
Signed-off-by: Sean Wang <sean.wang@mediatek.com>
Signed-off-by: Felix Fietkau <nbd@nbd.name>

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7615/Kconfig b/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7615/Kconfig
index e25db1135eda..c094260b0f89 100644
--- a/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7615/Kconfig
+++ b/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7615/Kconfig
@@ -35,6 +35,6 @@ config MT7663U
 	depends on MAC80211
 	depends on USB
 	help
-	  This adds support for MT7663U 802.11ax 2x2:2 wireless devices.
+	  This adds support for MT7663U 802.11ac 2x2:2 wireless devices.
 
 	  To compile this driver as a module, choose M here.
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7615/Kconfig`**
   - The description for the configuration option `MT7663U` was modified. 
   - The original text stated: "This adds support for MT7663U 802.11ax 2x2:2 wireless devices."
   - The updated text now correctly states: "This adds support for MT7663U 802.11ac 2x2:2 wireless devices."

### Relationships
- The modification in the Kconfig file corrects a typo regarding the wireless standard associated with the MT7663U device. The change clarifies that the MT7663U is an 802.11ac device instead of the previously incorrect 802.11ax designation. This fix is related to a prior commit (identified by the hash `eb99cc95c3b6`) that introduced support for the MT7663U, ensuring that the documentation accurately reflects the capabilities of the device.

mt76: mt7615: fix up typo in Kconfig for MT7663U

Fix up typo in Kconfig with indicating MT7663U is an 802.11ac device

Fixes: eb99cc95c3b6 ("mt76: mt7615: introduce mt7663u support")
Signed-off-by: Sean Wang <sean.wang@mediatek.com>
Signed-off-by: Felix Fietkau <nbd@nbd.name>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by a typographical error in the Kconfig file, where the wireless standard for the MT7663U device was incorrectly labeled as 802.11ax instead of the correct 802.11ac. This misrepresentation could lead to confusion regarding the capabilities of the device and potentially affect its configuration and usage in the system.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```plaintext
This adds support for MT7663U 802.11ac 2x2:2 wireless devices.
```
Reason:
The patch corrects the typo in the Kconfig file by changing the label from 802.11ax to 802.11ac, accurately reflecting the wireless standard supported by the MT7663U device, thus preventing potential confusion and ensuring proper configuration.
